practiceReport.name: DeVonta Smith
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Every-down starter workload (86% snaps) — 82% active conversion baseline when logging Limited Friday reps.
practiceReport.beatComment: Smith was targeted on 12 of Joe Milton's 21 passes in the wide receiver's first game since Week 6. Milton has thrown for just 310 yards without a touchdown pass through two starts for the Eagles, so expectations should be tempered for the team's passing game as a whole, but Smith has reclaimed his role as the team's top pass catcher. Smith could make the most of his hefty target share Thursday against the generous Dallas secondary.

practiceReport.name: Dallas Goedert
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Veteran starter profile (9th NFL season, 74% snap share) — elevated Questionable active conversion (84%) & Wednesday maintenance tolerance.
factors: Beat/podium consensus: on track to suit up
practiceReport.beatComment: Philadelphia deemed Goedert a limited participant on Monday's estimated injury report, but had the team held a traditional practice Tuesday, the veteran tight end would have been able to increase his activity. Goedert thus looks on track to play Thursday, when he'll face off against a Cowboys defense that he burned for five receptions for 48 yards on seven targets back in Week 7.

practiceReport.name: Saquon Barkley
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Perimeter speed/cut position (RB) — requires full deceleration/burst clearance on lower-body tags (76% Questionable baseline).
practiceReport.beatComment: Though Tuesday's injury report was merely an estimate, Barkley would have been able to take every rep had the Eagles held a traditional practice session. Barkley emerged from this past Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers with a neck injury and an illness, but neither health concern looks like it will prevent him from playing Thursday in Dallas.

practiceReport.name: Jalen Carter
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Every-down starter workload (84% snaps) — 82% active conversion baseline when logging Limited Friday reps.
practiceReport.beatComment: Carter informed the Eagles' medical staff while he was traveling to the stadium Sunday that his quadriceps was bothering him. The fifth-year defensive tackle has been cleared to suit up, but if he plays under a snap count or is available only as an emergency option, then Ty Robinson and Gabe Hall would be poised to take on larger roles on defense.

practiceReport.beatComment: Mitchell injured his left hamstring during the Eagles' 19-16 win over the Steelers on Sunday. He was held out of Monday's walkthrough practice but was back on the field in a limited capacity Tuesday, and defensive coordinator Vic Fangio told reporters that Mitchell should "be fine" to face the Cowboys on Thanksgiving Day. Riq Woolen would be in line for more defensive snaps in the event that Mitchell cannot play Thursday.

practiceReport.beatComment: Despite being listed as a limited participant throughout the week, Shipley made enough improvement in his recovery from an illness and his lingering plantar fascia injury to get the green light to play Thanksgiving Day. In his return from a four-game stint on injured reserve during last week's win over the Steelers, Shipley carried four times for nine yards while playing 19 of 53 snaps on offense.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Dameon Pierce
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Week 10 Bye excluded from NFL 4-game minimum count
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Pierce had been placed on injured reserve Oct. 28 due to an undisclosed issue. That was going to require him to miss at least four contests, but with the injury settlement, the veteran running back is now a free agent and is eligible to suit up as soon as he finds work with another club. Pierce appeared in three games with Philadelphia before being let go, rushing 37 times for 96 yards and two touchdowns while adding seven catches for 14 yards on 11 targets. He also took some turns as a kick returner, which could help him in his quest to latch on with another organization.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Tank Bigsby
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Bigsby will undergo core muscle surgery for an abdominal injury that he picked up during the Eagles' Week 4 loss to the Rams. The fourth-year pro will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 9 against the Giants. Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is also considered week-to-week, so with Bigsby on IR, Will Shipley could be the Eagles' starting running back for Week 5 against the Jaguars on Sunday in London.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Dontayvion Wicks
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Wicks missed the three games before the Eagles' Week 10 bye due to an ankle injury, and he was limited during Week 11 prep before the team tacked on a foot issue on Friday's practice report, after which he was ruled out for Sunday's contest against the Steelers. Per Tim McManus of ESPN.com, Wicks sustained the foot injury Friday, and it presumably led to his placement on IR. Wicks will be sidelined until at least Philadelphia's Week 15 matchup with Seattle on Saturday, Dec. 19.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Zack Baun
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Baun was held out of practice all week due to a back injury that he sustained against the Giants in Week 9. The injury is severe enough for him to require a stint on IR, which means he'll miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 15 against the Seahawks. Jeremiah Trotter figures to start alongside Jihaad Campbell at inside linebacker moving forward, beginning with Sunday's home tilt against the Steelers.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Andre' Sam
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: The Eagles waived Sam with an injury designation Sunday after he suffered a foot injury during Friday's preseason finale against the Bengals. The safety cleared waivers and will now spend the entirety of the 2026 regular season on IR unless he is waived with an injury designation.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Jalen Hurts
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Initially diagnosed with a superficial blood clot after being cleated in the left calf in an Oct. 4 loss to the Rams, Hurts had been cleared by doctors to play in Week 5 in the Eagles' loss to the Jaguars in London before more recent testing last week showed that the blood clot had moved. According to a statement released Monday by his agent, Nicole Lynn, Hurts now has been diagnosed with a deep vein thrombosis in the left calf, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. Hurts has gone on blood thinners to treat the blood clots, and while his prognosis is good and he's not expected to face any long-term health effects, he won't be able to participate in football activities until he's off blood thinners. With that in mind, Hurts isn't expected to make a push for a late-season return from injured reserve and instead will turn his focus toward returning to full health in 2027. The Eagles will move forward with Tanner McKee, Cole Payton and Joe Milton as their options at quarterback.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Johnny Wilson
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Wilson was let go by Philadelphia on Friday but is set to return to the team after clearing waivers, albeit on injured reserve. The 25-year-old will now be forced to miss the entirety of the upcoming campaign unless he's waived with an injury settlement.

irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Castro-Fields' tenure with the Eagles has come to an end after he first signed with the team's practice squad last October. He will now look to get healthy and catch on with another team.
